en: The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo lowered global temperatures by about 0.5 degrees Celsius for over a year.
Pumice is the only rock that floats on water because it is full of tiny trapped gas bubbles.
The Moon drifts away from Earth at 3.8 centimeters per year, which is the same speed your fingernails grow.
A neutron star is so incredibly dense that one teaspoon of its material would weigh six billion tons.
Saturn is the only planet in our solar system less dense than water, meaning it would theoretically float.
A single large thundercloud can weigh over one million pounds because of all its suspended liquid water droplets.
It rains solid diamonds on Neptune and Uranus because extreme atmospheric pressure crushes carbon atoms into gemstones.
Mayon Volcano in the Philippines has erupted over 50 times since 1616, making it one of the most active.
The solid inner core of the Earth is as hot as the surface of the Sun, reaching 5,400 degrees Celsius.
The strongest wind gust ever recorded on Earth reached 253 miles per hour during Tropical Cyclone Olivia in 1996.
Jupiter’s Great Red Spot is a massive storm wider than Earth that has been continuously raging for 350 years.
Groundwater makes up about 30 percent of all freshwater on Earth, while rivers and lakes hold less than one percent.
